get.description:
## Overview
Returns the contact-level availability of every communication channel the business has (email, SMS, and installed third-party apps) for a single contact. Each entry reports whether the contact can be reached on that channel and, when not, a machine-readable reason.

The business is resolved from the caller's staff context; the contact must belong to that business.

Available for **Staff Tokens**

parameters.name: contact_uid
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the contact (client) to evaluate channel availability for (e.g., "peu8ljecwqr5ok58").

success.description: Indicates whether the API request was successful (true) or failed (false).

data.description: The response payload. Present on successful responses (success: true).

error.description: Error message for simple error responses. Used in some legacy endpoints.

errors.description: Array of error objects for detailed error responses. Present on error responses (success: false).

field.description: The field that caused the error (for validation errors).

allOf.description: Generic wrapper object for API responses. Success responses contain 'data', while error responses contain 'errors' array or 'error' string.

contact_channels.description: Availability of each communication channel the business has for the requested contact.

items.description: Represents the availability of a single communication channel for a specific contact. It combines the business-level capability of the channel with a contact-level eligibility check, so callers can decide how to reach a contact in one lookup. This is a computed, read-only resource (evaluated on request) and therefore has no uid, business_uid, or timestamps.

channel_uid.description: Unique identifier of the channel. For the core channels this is the fixed email/sms channel UID; for third-party apps it is the business channel UID, so multiple channels of the same app can be told apart and targeted individually. Treat this as an opaque value returned by the API rather than one to hardcode.

channel.description: Identifier of the communication channel. Core channels are "email" and "sms"; installed third-party apps use their app code name (e.g., "facebook", "whatsapp", "instagram"). The set of possible values grows as new apps are installed, so treat this as an open string rather than a fixed enum. Note: a business can have multiple channels of the same app, so this value is not unique within the response — use channel_uid to distinguish them.

display_name.description: Human-readable name of the channel as set by the business (e.g., a specific Facebook page or WhatsApp number name). Null for the core email and sms channels.

available.description: Whether the contact can currently be reached on this channel. True only when both the business supports the channel and the contact is individually eligible.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason the channel is unavailable. Null when the channel is available. Possible values: "no_email" (contact has no email address), "email_blocked" (email is bounced/blocked and cannot receive), "no_phone" (contact has no mobile phone number), "opted_out" (contact opted out of transactional SMS), "no_active_session" (third-party channel has no active session for the contact), "app_not_installed" (business does not have the channel enabled/installed).

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

404.description: Not Found - The contact does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated business

## Overview
Creates a Message.

Available for **Staff and Directory tokens**. Directory tokens require the `X-On-Behalf-Of` header with the target business UID.

channels.description: Comma-separated list of delivery channels (e.g., "sms", "email"). When omitted, the message is sent to all available channels.

client_id.description: The UID of the recipient client. Required to identify the target contact and resolve the conversation.

conversation_title.description: Title for the conversation. Optional; used when creating a new conversation.

conversation_uid.description: UID of an existing conversation to add the message to. If omitted, the system creates or uses the client's default conversation.

direction.description: The direction of the message. Required. Valid values: "client_to_business", "business_to_client".

staff_id.description: UID of the staff member sending the message. Optional — if omitted, the staff is auto-assigned based on business assignment rules.

text.description: The text content of the message. Required. Plain text only — do not include HTML tags.

## Overview
Create a new business' communication channel. Available for **Staff, App, and Directory tokens**.

**Note:** Channels start with a `pending` status upon creation. They are activated asynchronously via a webhook callback from the communication-gw to the calling application. The channel will transition to `active` status only after the webhook activation event is received and processed.

delete.description:
## Overview
Deletes an existing channel. Available for **Staff, App, and Directory tokens**.

**Note:** Channels follow an async webhook-based lifecycle. Channels start as `pending` and are activated asynchronously via webhook callback from the communication-gw.

put.description:

parameters.name: activity_type
parameters.description: Filter by activity type. Limits results to messages associated with a specific type of business activity (e.g., "meeting", "invoice", "payment", "announcement").

parameters.name: activity_action
parameters.description: Filter by the specific action or status of the activity (e.g., "scheduled", "created", "cancelled"). Available values depend on the activity_type.

parameters.name: client_uid
parameters.description: Filter by client unique identifier. Returns only activity messages associated with the specified client.

parameters.name: staff_uid
parameters.description: Filter by staff unique identifier. Returns only activity messages associated with the specified staff member.

parameters.name: conversation_uid
parameters.description: Filter by conversation unique identifier. Returns only activity messages that belong to the specified conversation thread.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Filter by message direction. Use "business_to_client" for messages sent from the business to the client, or "client_to_business" for messages sent from the client to the business. Note: the response returns the raw direction values which include four possible values: "pivot_to_client" (business sent to client), "client_to_pivot" (client sent to business), "to_pivot" (system notification to the business side), and "to_client" (system notification to the client side). The filter values "business_to_client" and "client_to_business" match against "pivot_to_client" and "client_to_pivot" respectively.

parameters.name: was_read
parameters.description: Filter by read status. Set to "true" to return only messages that have been read, or "false" for unread messages.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Filter messages created on or after this date. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z").

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Filter messages created on or before this date. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., "2026-03-01T23:59:59Z").

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order for results in the format "field:direction" (e.g., "created_at:desc" or "created_at:asc"). Defaults to "created_at:desc" if not specified.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page. Maximum value is 100.

success.description: Indicates whether the API request was successful (true) or failed (false).

data.description: The response payload. Present on successful responses (success: true).

error.description: Error message for simple error responses. Used in some legacy endpoints.

errors.description: Array of error objects for detailed error responses. Present on error responses (success: false).

field.description: The field that caused the error (for validation errors).

allOf.description: Generic wrapper object for API responses. Success responses contain 'data', while error responses contain 'errors' array or 'error' string.

activity_messages.description: List of activity message records matching the query filters.

items.description: Represents an activity message associated with a business-client interaction. Activity messages are created automatically by the system for various activity types (e.g., meetings, invoices, payments) or manually via the invite activity type. Each message captures the communication context including direction, channels, and activity-specific metadata.

uid.description: Unique identifier for the activity message record.

business_uid.description: Unique identifier of the business associated with this activity message.

## Overview
Updates a single conversation. This endpoint is used for several distinct operations against the same conversation resource:

- Archive / unarchive
- Mark as spam / not spam
- Mark as read / unread for the business side (`business_unread`)
- Soft delete (`deleted`)
- **Create, update, complete, or remove a follow-up reminder for the requesting staff member**

All fields are optional in the request body — send only the fields you want to change. Only fields that are present in the request body are evaluated.

Available for **Staff tokens**.

## Follow-up flow

Follow-ups in vcita are scoped to a single staff member on a single conversation, and are stored on the underlying `Collaborator` record (per staff/conversation), not on the conversation itself. Sending follow-up fields on this endpoint always operates on the follow-up record of the **staff identified by the bearer token**.

The endpoint branches based on the combination of `follow_up` and `archived` in the request body:

| Sent fields | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `follow_up: true`, no `archived` (or `archived: false`) | **Create or update** a follow-up for the requesting staff. Creates a Collaborator if one does not already exist. Sets `follow_up=true`, `follow_up_message`, and optionally `follow_up_date`. If the conversation was archived, it is automatically unarchived. If a `follow_up_message` is provided without a `follow_up_date`, an internal text message is added to the conversation. |
| `follow_up: true`, `archived: true` | **Remove** the follow-up (used to dismiss/snooze). If `complete_follow_up: true` is also sent, the follow-up is marked as completed. |
| `follow_up: false` | **Remove** the follow-up. If `complete_follow_up: true` is also sent, the follow-up is marked as completed. |

Note: The follow-up branch only fires when the request body actually contains a `follow_up` key, and the add/remove logic only fires when the new `follow_up` value differs from the current one (with the exception of the `follow_up: true, archived: true` case, which always removes).

## Permitted update fields

Fields outside of the follow-up flow are permitted via `Conversation::READ_WRITE_PARAMS`: `archived`, `business_unread`, `spam`, `deleted`, `campaign`, `source_type`, `mobile`. The follow-up fields (`follow_up`, `follow_up_date`, `follow_up_message`, `complete_follow_up`) are read separately from the request body and are not part of the permitted attributes list.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier (uid) of the conversation to update (e.g., "89m2pnabgozdvd9f"). If the uid points to a conversation that has been merged into another, the request is automatically routed to the merged target conversation.

parameters.name: full_client
parameters.description: When set to a truthy value, the response client object is rendered in its full representation (instead of the default summary), and the conversation is rendered in its deep representation (adds source/source_data/source_type/sourceable fields and sets `depth` to "deep").

200.description: Conversation updated successfully. Returns the updated conversation as decorated by ConversationDecorator. Note that `follow_up_date` and `follow_up_message` on the response reflect the values sent in the request (they are exposed on the conversation via accessors but persisted on the per-staff Collaborator record).

example.title: Jane Smith
example.follow_up_text: Reminder set for tomorrow at 1:31 PM

401.description: Unauthorized. The bearer token is missing, invalid, expired, or not a staff token.

403.description: Forbidden. The authenticated staff is not allowed to update this conversation (Pundit policy denied access).

errors.message: You are not authorized to perform this action.

404.description: Not Found. No conversation with the given uid exists, or the conversation belongs to a different business than the one resolved from the bearer token.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity. The follow-up validation failed. The most common cause is `follow_up_date` being in the past; the staff resolved from the bearer token could not be found is also possible.

schema.description: Partial update payload. All fields are optional; send only the fields you want to change.

follow_up.description: Whether a follow-up should be active on this conversation for the requesting staff. Setting this field is what triggers the follow-up branch. Set to `true` to create/update a follow-up, or `false` to remove it. When combined with `archived: true`, `follow_up: true` removes the follow-up (used to dismiss it from the inbox).

follow_up_date.description: When the follow-up reminder should fire. Accepts any string parseable by Ruby's Time parser, including the JavaScript-style format the UI sends (e.g., "Wed May 06 2026 13:31:21 GMT+0300 (Israel Daylight Time)") and ISO 8601 (e.g., "2026-05-06T10:31:21Z"). Must be in the future. Only consumed when creating/updating a follow-up.

follow_up_message.description: Free-text note attached to the follow-up (e.g., "just a test", "call back about pricing"). Defaults to an empty string. When a non-empty `follow_up_message` is sent without a `follow_up_date`, an internal text message is automatically added to the conversation as a record of the follow-up note.

complete_follow_up.description: Only meaningful when removing a follow-up (i.e., `follow_up: false`, or `follow_up: true` with `archived: true`). When `true`, the follow-up is marked as completed rather than simply dismissed.

archived.description: Archive (`true`) or unarchive (`false`) the conversation. When sent together with `follow_up: true`, it instead removes the follow-up (see the follow-up branching table above).

business_unread.description: Mark the conversation as unread (`true`) or read (`false`) for the business side. When this field is present, the read state is propagated to the relevant staff collaboration record.

spam.description: Mark the conversation as spam (`true`) or not spam (`false`). When set, the spam state is also applied to the associated client.

deleted.description: Soft-delete (`true`) the conversation (sets `deleted_at` to the current time). Hard deletion is performed via the DELETE endpoint, not via this field.

campaign.description: Free-form campaign tag stored on the conversation.

mobile.description: Internal flag indicating whether the conversation originated from a mobile device.

Purchase a phone number from a telecom provider and assign it to a business account. features.description: List of telephony features to enable for this phone number, (e.g., ["VOICE", "SMS"]).

verification_request_data.description: Business verification information required for text messaging compliance in the United States and Canada. This data registers your business with mobile carriers to enable SMS messaging capabilities. The verification process helps prevent spam and ensures your business messages are delivered reliably to customers.

NON_PROFIT: Non-profit organization (e.g., 501(c)(3)). SOLE_PROPRIETOR: Individual business owner without formal business entity.

street.description: Street address and number (e.g., "123 Main Street", "456 5th Avenue")

full_address.description: Complete formatted address including street, city, state, postal code, and country (e.g., "123 Main Street, New York, NY 10001, USA")
